citation: R. León Lira, L. Güereca and J. Lekube, “Life cycle assessment of wave energy: The Mutriku case study,” J. Ocean Eng. Mar. Energy, vol. 12, no. 3, pp. 1525–1542, 2026, doi: 10.1007/s40722-026-00487-0.
used_for: 226 g CO2e/kWh; stage split 195 / 12.4 / 17.9 g (86.6% / 5.5% / 7.9%); 20-year model life; 4.93 GWh; energy payback 26.2 years; 53–94% more greenhouse gas than other ocean devices; PV 8 years and wind 1.5 years quoted for comparison; materials (about 12.9 kt concrete, 21.3 kt limestone); recycling scenarios E1–E3; dismantling assumed zero; breakwater maintenance excluded; data sources (secondary databases, Mutriku staff).
source_location: Abstract (86.6%, 5.5%, recycling note). Results: climate-change table and stage split. Section 2.4 and 3.1 (inventory 'provided by the Mutriku staff'). Table 2 (material quantities in kg). Fig. 7 discussion ('between 53 and 94% more'). EPBT paragraph (cites Aman et al. 2015 for 8 and 1.5 years). Table 4 and the recycling scenario text. In the PDF, search for the phrases '53 and 94', 'Energy Payback Time', 'lack of data' and 'Mutriku staff'.
review: Full text and relevant model sections reviewed.
limits: Modelled impacts and preliminary payback. Dismantling is omitted; text/Table 4 recycling rankings differ. Figure 7 is not a harmonised comparison.

citation: G. Ibarra-Berastegi, J. Sáenz, A. Ulazia, P. Serras, G. Esnaola and C. García-Soto, “Electricity production, capacity factor, and plant efficiency index at the Mutriku wave farm (2014–2016),” Ocean Eng., vol. 147, pp. 20–29, 2018, doi: 10.1016/j.oceaneng.2017.10.018.
used_for: 14 turbines analysed; about 10 working on average; 246,468.7 kWh per year for 2014–2016; capacity factor about 0.11.
source_location: Abstract (all four figures are in the abstract on the repository page).
review: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record reviewed; full operating dataset not reanalysed.
limits: 2014–2016 observations, not current performance. Author spelling corrected to Ulazia. The 14-turbine study configuration differs from the 16-position design.

citation: Basque Government, “La planta de Mutriku, primera comercial europea que genera energía con las olas, ha producido en un año 200.000 kWh,” Irekia, Aug. 12, 2012 (in Spanish).
used_for: First-year output about 200,000 kWh; plant inaugurated 7 July 2011; storm in December 2011 damaged the control building and stopped the plant until March 2012; about 500 requests to visit; 600,000 kWh a year expected in the second year.
source_location: Body of the news item (the reprint attributes the figures to the Basque Government's Industry Department).
review: Original government announcement reviewed; dated 12 August 2012.
limits: Historical forecast, shutdown and visit context. Its 15-turbine/300 kW description is not used for the design specification.

citation: L. Gato et al., “Sea trial results of the biradial and Wells turbines at Mutriku wave power plant,” Energy Convers. Manag., vol. 268, Art. no. 115936, 2022, doi: 10.1016/j.enconman.2022.115936.
used_for: Turbine sea trials carried out at the Mutriku plant, showing that the plant is also used as a turbine test site.
source_location: Title and abstract.
review: Article abstract and publication metadata reviewed.
limits: 37% is a relative gain in mean time-averaged peak efficiency during trials, not demonstrated annual whole-plant output.

citation: J. Bald et al., “The contribution of the SafeWAVE EU project to the future development of ocean energy,” Int. Mar. Energy J., vol. 8, pp. 73–82, 2025, doi: 10.36688/imej.8.73-82.
used_for: Recommends early and ongoing engagement with communities; reports no clear rise in sound pressure about 1 km from the Mutriku plant when it operates; says it is still too early for robust conclusions.
source_location: Abstract and sections on stakeholder engagement and on underwater sound; the Mutriku statement is in the sound results. In the PDF, search for 'Mutriku' and 'early and often'.
review: Full paper reviewed, including p. 76 and monitoring table.
limits: The 1,000 m statement and other-site ecological findings retain their scope; later publication does not imply an independent repeat campaign.

citation: I. Heras-Saizarbitoria, I. Zamanillo and I. Laskurain, “Social acceptance of ocean wave energy: A case study of an OWC shoreline plant,” Renew. Sustain. Energy Rev., vol. 27, pp. 515–524, 2013, doi: 10.1016/j.rser.2013.07.032.
used_for: Studies community acceptance of the Mutriku plant and concludes that effective and meaningful social involvement is important.
source_location: Abstract.
review: Full article retrieved; abstract, case-study discussion and conclusions checked.
limits: Historical qualitative acceptance study. Later SafeWAVE engagement is relevant but is not a directly comparable current acceptance survey.

citation: L. Johanning, “The fascinating history of wave energy,” WEDUSEA, Jun. 3, 2025.
used_for: Bochaux-Praceique built what is believed to be the first oscillating water column (1910); Masuda's wave-powered navigation buoy (1940s); LIMPET installed in 2000 and operated successfully for over 10 years.
source_location: Main article text (history section).
review: Project history article reviewed.
limits: Historical context; not a peer-reviewed paper. Priority claims are attributed and qualified.

citation: IEA-OES, “First generation devices,” Ocean Energy Systems, n.d.
used_for: Wells turbine invented in the late 1970s; full-size OWC prototype at Toftestallen, Norway, 1985; Pico (1999) and LIMPET (2000).
source_location: Section on oscillating water column devices.
review: IEA-OES technical history page reviewed.
limits: Historical technology overview, not an assessment of current Mutriku performance.

citation: International WaTERS, “Mutriku Area,” European Marine Energy Centre and Ocean Energy Systems, n.d.
used_for: The Mutriku site is designed for testing power take-off systems including air turbines; it lists an 18.5 kW generator and a grid connection; operational since 2011.
source_location: Main page text and specification list.
review: Test-site entry reviewed; working .html address found.
limits: Facility capability, not evidence of measured environmental benefit or present availability.

citation: Tethys, “Mutriku Wave Power Plant,” Tethys Knowledge Base, n.d.
used_for: Construction noise reportedly heard 3–10 km away and concerned the local population; no complaints in about 10 years of operation; 2016 survey found no evidence of significant acoustic impact but noted limitations; hard-bottom habitat at 4–6 m depth; breakwater may change sediment transport and flow but the OWC adds no significant difference.
source_location: Environmental effects and monitoring text, and the physical-conditions table, on the project page.
review: Developer-supplied record and monitoring entries reviewed; page updated 1 July 2025.
limits: Includes limited surveys, developer reports and stale report-availability text. Use the newer report [18] for the 2022 campaign results.

citation: L. Frayer, “Spain expands renewables with wave-powered electricity plant,” NPR, Nov. 26, 2012.
used_for: The breakwater was built to protect the harbour and the plant is housed inside it; the turbines are not in contact with seawater; cost just under $3 million not counting the breakwater.
source_location: Body of the article.
review: NPR report as republished by WFAE reviewed.
limits: Historical journalism. The title follows the linked WFAE edition; technical salt-exposure claims are supported by [15].

citation: I. Muxika, P. Vinagre and J. Bald, “Deliverable 2.4: Monitoring of seafloor integrity,” WESE project, Nov. 30, 2020.
used_for: 'The Mutriku Wave Power Plant operates in a breakwater, on artificial substrata'; no seafloor integrity monitoring is reported for Mutriku.
source_location: Description of the monitored sites; in the PDF search for 'Mutriku' and 'artificial substrata'.
review: Report and its Mutriku scope statement reviewed.
limits: The body focuses seafloor findings on MARMOK-A-5 and WaveRoller. Artificial breakwater substrate does not establish no surrounding habitat effects.

citation: EVE, “The Mutriku wave plant achieves cumulative electricity production of three million kilowatts per hour,” Jan. 11, 2024.
used_for: January 2024 announcement of the 3 GWh milestone, 12.5 years, approximately 300 MWh/year and EVE’s attributed historical claims.
source_location: Headline and body of the release.
review: EVE announcement of 11 January 2024 reviewed; duplicate BiMEP version consolidated here.
limits: 3 GWh milestone and about 300 MWh/year are operator reports with different bases. 240 is rounded author arithmetic, not an exact source-reported annual mean.

citation: Interreg Europe, “BIMEP (Mutriku): World’s first breakwater wave power plant: acceptance of the community,” n.d.
used_for: As cited on the poster for the plant, milestone, visits and community context. Use [10, 13, 19–21] for independently accessible evidence.
source_location: Main text of the good-practice page.
review: Retained from the supplied workbook; direct access returned HTTP 403.
limits: Not independently verified in this review. The 13-year complaint account remains unverified. EVE [20] corroborates the end-2023 milestone and the Geopark [21] lists the visit.

citation: J. Lopez-Mendia, A. Aristondo, P. Ricci, J. Lekube, S. Ceballos and E. Robles, “Improving the power production of Mutriku Wave Power Plant throughout tuning the actual generator and damping valve limits,” Ocean Eng., vol. 315, Art. no. 119917, 2025, doi: 10.1016/j.oceaneng.2024.119917.
used_for: Reports 'exposure to a saline environment' causing material fatigue, Wells turbine and generator failures from salt-water exposure, salt accumulation in the cooling system, and corrosion and splashing of the mechanical and electrical parts in high waves.

review: Full PDF reviewed for failure mechanisms, salt exposure and control-study scope.
limits: Numerical control gains and thermal limits need validation; no percentage has been added to historical annual plant output.

citation: Basque Government, “Euskadi dispone ya de la primera planta europea que suministra energía a través de las olas,” Irekia, Jul. 7, 2011 (in Spanish).
used_for: 16 chambers, 296 kW, €6.7M total project cost with €2.3M for the energy installation, and 600 MWh a year expected.
source_location: Body of the 7 July 2011 release (checked earlier in this work).
review: Exact 7 July 2011 government announcement located and reviewed.
limits: €6.7M total project and €2.3M energy installation are historical capital figures, not current costs or LCOE.

citation: Offshore Energy, “Mutriku wave plant hits 2GWh mark,” Offshore Energy, Feb. 24, 2020.
used_for: Mutriku reached 2 GWh (announced 24 Feb 2020); in 2016, five years after commissioning, it became the first plant of its kind to produce 1 GWh.
source_location: First paragraphs of the article.
review: Correct article address located; accessible page omitted the article body. Milestones corroborated against the primary BiMEP announcement.
limits: 1 GWh in 2016 and 2 GWh announced in February 2020; cumulative totals do not establish an annual time series.

citation: E. Le Bourhis et al., “Deliverable 2.6: Data results and analysis towards impacts’ evaluation,” SafeWAVE project, Dec. 17, 2024.
used_for: One-month operational-phase acoustic campaign at Mutriku in March–April 2022; one of three hydrophones did not work properly; 'No contribution to the background soundscape from the WEC was observed'; seabed, electromagnetic and fish monitoring are not covered for Mutriku.
source_location: Acoustic chapter, Mutriku section. In the PDF search for 'Mutriku' and 'hydrophone'.
review: SafeWAVE Deliverable 2.6 reviewed, especially printed p. 24.
limits: One March–April 2022 operational campaign; one hydrophone malfunctioned. No detected contribution is not proof of zero sound or ecological effects.

source_location: About the Mutriku site; Technical Characteristics
review: Official operator specification reviewed; retained from the earlier website.
